title: SDK interoperability shims and canonical examples for streaming + tool-calls + structured output
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create language-idiomatic shim layers and a small canonical example package for TypeScript, Python, and Go that demonstrate: 1) streaming generation with backpressure-friendly APIs, 2) first-class tool/function calling (sync+async), and 3) structured JSON/typed outputs with schema validation. The goal is to produce reference libraries and examples that client SDKs can adopt to provide consistent behavior and ergonomic migration paths from older SDK surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Three example repos (TS, Py, Go) that implement the shim and include a minimal app demonstrating streaming generation, a tool call (file-search or calculator), and schema-validated structured output.
A2: Clear API contract document (one-pager) that lists guarantees: event ordering, resume semantics, error classification, and idempotency for tool calls.
A3: Migration guide showing how to adapt existing non-streaming code to the shim with >1 practical code snippet per language.
A4: Unit and integration test matrix that exercises backpressure (slow consumer), tool failure and retry, and schema regression checks.
A5: Internal review and sign-off from DX lead and Runtime API owner.

implementation_notes: Shim model: keep core client stable; expose thin adapter that wraps existing client request/response. Adapter responsibilities: framing -> language stream primitives, tool call orchestration, schema validation hooks, and resume token handling.
TypeScript: async generator + EventEmitter hybrid to support both for-await-of and on('event') patterns. Prefer optional zod validator; if absent, fallback to shallow JSON shape checks.
Python: async iterator (PEP 525) with context manager support for automatic cancellation on exit. Use optional pydantic BaseModel for schema validation.
Go: channel-based streamer with context.Context cancellation and a small helper for incremental JSON decode. Use gojsonschema as optional dependency; avoid heavy reflection.
Tool calling: define a common 'ToolSpec' that includes name, input_schema, run_mode (sync|async), and idempotency hints. The shim will translate tool call events to language-native callable handles.

Error model: map runtime error codes to three classes: transient (retry with backoff), permanent (bubble to caller), and tool-failure (return structured failure object). Document retry policy defaults and override hooks.
Compatibility: provide migration helpers that adapt older blocking RPC calls into the streaming shim using a small adapter that buffers until first flush token or timeout.
Testing: add consumer-sim tests that emulate slow readers, tool timeouts, and partial JSON emissions to validate robustness.
Telemetry: emit lightweight events for 'shim-invocation', 'tool-call-start', 'tool-call-finish', and 'schema-violation' with sampling defaults. Ensure PHI/PII filter guidance in docs.
Packaging: examples published under examples/redwood-sdk-shims/<lang> with README, quickstart, and a sample app (calculator + file indexer).
